kind: frozen distractor-rich cross-page research retrieval evaluation

design.ordinary_distractor_text: Legacy ordinary memory {index}: Python memory management JavaScript asynchronous runtime performance browser storage caching offline applications.
design.seed_order: All 60 ordinary memories are inserted before any research projection; research memories are saved in save_order.
design.relevance_labels: Binary labels predeclared per query from source content, independent of the retrieval scorer.
design.analysis_mode: Local synthetic fixture; historical corpus analyses use owner_correction=true because the controlled corpus intentionally spans each goal. No external provider is called.

goals.instruction: Understand Python memory management and garbage collection
Assess browser storage and caching for offline applications

memories.title: Historical source P01
memories.text: CPython uses reference counting to reclaim most objects immediately when their reference count reaches zero.

memories.title: Historical source P02
memories.text: The cyclic garbage collector detects reference cycles among container objects that reference counting cannot reclaim.

memories.title: Historical source P03
memories.text: A generational collector separates short-lived objects from long-lived ones to shorten full collection pauses.

memories.title: Historical source P04
memories.text: The global interpreter lock prevents multiple threads from executing Python bytecode in parallel.

memories.title: Historical source P05
memories.text: A memory arena allocator obtains large blocks from the operating system and subdivides them for small objects.

memories.title: Historical source P06
memories.text: Weak references allow caches to observe objects without preventing their collection.

memories.title: Historical source P07
memories.text: The __slots__ declaration avoids per-instance dictionaries and reduces object memory overhead.

memories.title: Historical source P08
memories.text: Object headers store a reference count and a pointer to the type object.

memories.title: Historical source P09
memories.text: Tracing collectors follow pointers from roots instead of counting references.

memories.title: Historical source P10
memories.text: Finalizers run during collection and can resurrect objects by storing a new reference.

memories.title: Historical source P11
memories.text: Arena fragmentation can retain freed memory in pools for later reuse.

memories.title: Historical source P12
memories.text: The garbage collector is disabled during interpreter finalization.

memories.title: Historical source J01
memories.text: The event loop moves completed promise callbacks from the microtask queue to the call stack before the next macrotask.

memories.title: Historical source J02
memories.text: Promise resolution schedules reactions as microtasks, so they run before timers.

memories.title: Historical source J03
memories.text: requestAnimationFrame batches visual updates before the browser repaints.

memories.title: Historical source J04
memories.text: Long tasks block the main thread and delay input responsiveness.

memories.title: Historical source J05
memories.text: Web Workers run scripts on a separate thread and communicate by message passing.

memories.title: Historical source J06
memories.text: The call stack executes synchronous JavaScript one frame at a time.

memories.title: Historical source J07
memories.text: The macrotask queue holds timer callbacks and runs them after microtasks complete in each event loop turn.

memories.title: Historical source J08
memories.text: Debouncing delays a function until input events stop for a fixed interval.

memories.title: Historical source J09
memories.text: Layout thrashing occurs when reads and writes alternate and force synchronous reflow.

memories.title: Historical source J10
memories.text: The browser may coalesce DOM mutations into a single visual rendering update.

memories.title: Historical source J11
memories.text: A synthetic benchmark measured event-loop lag during a CPU-bound loop.

memories.title: Historical source J12
memories.text: Service workers intercept network requests and can serve cached responses.

memories.title: Historical source B01
memories.text: The Cache API stores request and response pairs that service workers can read offline.

memories.title: Historical source B02
memories.text: IndexedDB provides a transactional object store for structured client-side data.

memories.title: Historical source B03
memories.text: localStorage offers synchronous string key-value persistence with a small quota.

memories.title: Historical source B04
memories.text: The HTTP cache honours response headers such as Cache-Control and ETag.

memories.title: Historical source B05
memories.text: Service workers precache application shell assets during installation for offline use.

memories.title: Historical source B06
memories.text: Quota management evicts origin data when storage pressure grows.

memories.title: Historical source B07
memories.text: IndexedDB transactions abort when a request fails unless handled.

memories.title: Historical source B08
memories.text: Session storage clears when the browser tab closes.

memories.title: Historical source B09
memories.text: Cookies are sent with HTTP requests and have size limits.

memories.title: Historical source B10
memories.text: Cache storage is origin-scoped, stores request-response pairs, and persists offline across browser sessions.

memories.title: Historical source B11
memories.text: A manifest file declares installability metadata for a progressive web app.

memories.title: Historical source B12
memories.text: ETag revalidation avoids downloading an unchanged response body.

queries.text: Reference counting reclaims objects immediately when their count reaches zero, but cycles need another mechanism.
queries.label_rationale: Both sources describe reference counting and the cycle-collection problem named by the query.

queries.text: Generational collection separates short-lived objects from long-lived ones to shorten full collection pauses.
queries.label_rationale: The source describes generational collection, short-lived and long-lived objects, and pause reduction.

queries.text: Python's global interpreter lock prevents multiple threads from executing bytecode in parallel.
queries.label_rationale: The source describes the global interpreter lock and parallel bytecode execution.

queries.text: Quantum stabilizer codes protect logical qubits from decoherence.
queries.label_rationale: No retained source for this goal discusses quantum error correction; the correct outcome is abstention.

queries.text: Promise reactions run as microtasks before timers and the next macrotask.
queries.label_rationale: All three sources describe microtask, promise-reaction, timer or macrotask ordering.

queries.text: Animation frame callbacks batch visual updates before the browser repaints.
queries.label_rationale: Both sources describe frame-aligned visual updates or coalesced rendering before repaint.

queries.text: A long task blocks the main thread and delays input responsiveness.
queries.label_rationale: The source describes long tasks blocking the main thread and delaying input.

queries.text: The database normalized schema removes redundant columns.
queries.label_rationale: No retained source for this goal discusses relational schema normalization; the correct outcome is abstention.

queries.text: A service worker reads cache request-response pairs offline after precaching the app shell.
queries.label_rationale: All three sources describe service-worker caching, precached shell assets or offline cache storage.

queries.text: IndexedDB transactions store structured records and abort when a request fails.
queries.label_rationale: Both sources describe IndexedDB transactions, structured object stores and request failure behaviour.

queries.text: Storage pressure triggers quota eviction of origin data while localStorage has a small synchronous quota.
queries.label_rationale: One source describes quota eviction under storage pressure; the other describes localStorage's small synchronous quota.

queries.text: The compiler optimizes tail calls in functional languages.
queries.label_rationale: No retained source for this goal discusses compilers or tail calls; the correct outcome is abstention.

arms.A_recency: Eligible same-goal active research rows sorted by reviewed_at descending, then ID; top 3.
arms.B_alive12_unscoped: Frozen ALIVE-12 behaviour: MemoryService query built from the goal and current text, top_k*5 candidates, then post-filter by research metadata, goal, active status, current URL/SHA and SHA deduplication.
arms.C_corrected_scoped_lexical: ALIVE-13 scoped lexical ranker over authoritative research rows; scope by instance, goal and active status before scoring; score 2*current-content overlap + goal-term overlap; deterministic recency then ID tie-break; top 3 after deduplication.
arms.D_full_history_access: All eligible same-goal active research rows with no ranking or limit; used only to distinguish access to history from ranking among it.

success_criteria.crowding_regression: C retrieves at least one predeclared relevant memory for every positive query despite 60 ordinary memories and 35 competing research memories.
success_criteria.classification_rule: RETRIEVAL_ADVANTAGE_DEMONSTRATED only if every criterion above passes; otherwise NO_RETRIEVAL_ADVANTAGE_DEMONSTRATED or INCONCLUSIVE as stated in the evidence.

caveats: The corpus is lexical and controlled; it does not establish semantic paraphrase or owner-perceived usefulness.
Relevance labels are source-adequacy labels, not task outcomes or independent human ratings.
The corrected ranker is deterministic and makes no embedding or model call.
The old arm intentionally reproduces the pre-ALIVE-13 unscoped query and post-filter order.
The full-history arm is a control, not a retrievable product mode.
No paid inference is used; synthetic note generation is a local fixture.
